claims.quote: Manual annotation is costly, time-consuming, and often impractical, particularly in specialized domains such as histopathology ref [1], medical imaging ref [16], and industrial inspection ref [39].

Self-supervised representation learning (SSRL) addresses this challenge by exploiting the intrinsic structure of unlabeled data to generate supervisory signals automatically ref [27], eliminating reliance on human-provided labels.
Contrastive learning methods subsequently emerged as dominant paradigms, leveraging instance discrimination objectives across visual ref [27], temporal ref [2], and graph-structured data ref [19].

A **pretext task** is a self-defined auxiliary objective—such as rotation prediction ref [12], jigsaw puzzle solving ref [10], or masked reconstruction ref [4]—that generates supervisory signals from unlabeled data.

The Context Autoencoder (CAE) ref [4] advances masked image modeling (MIM) by predicting representations of masked patches in encoded space via an encoder–regressor–decoder architecture, encouraging separation between representation learning and reconstruction.

MOKD further advances this framework by enabling two heterogeneous models to learn collaboratively through self-distillation and cross-distillation modes, enhancing semantic alignment via cross-attention feature search ref [56].

Point2Vec ref [15] extends the data2vec masked student-teacher framework to point cloud domains, identifying that positional information leakage reveals object shape under heavy masking and proposing targeted solutions to address this 3D-specific shortcoming.

In astronomical imaging, contrastive learning applied to multiband galaxy photometry enables morphology classification and photometric redshift estimation, outperforming supervised baselines with two to four times fewer labels ref [58].

Graph Barlow Twins eliminates the need for negative samples entirely by employing a cross-correlation-based loss, achieving competitive performance while requiring substantially fewer hyperparameters and approximately 30 times faster computation than BGRL ref [19].

TimesURL addresses limitations in positive/negative pair construction through frequency-temporal augmentation and double Universum hard negatives, achieving state-of-the-art performance across six downstream tasks including forecasting, imputation, classification, and anomaly detection ref [17].

CCBERT (Code Change BERT) exemplifies this direction by pretraining a Transformer-based model on large-scale unlabeled code change repositories using four specialized self-supervised objectives that capture token-level edit actions between old and new code versions ref [30].

A comprehensive review of self-supervised speech representation learning ref [23] identifies multi-modal pretraining—combining speech with text or visual streams—as a distinct and productive category.
